result.title: Density-Aware Calibration for Resource-Efficient Medical Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) show promise for clinical image understanding, but their computational and memory requirements hinder deployment on resource-constrained clinical hardware. Post-training quantization (PTQ) offers a practical compression strategy without retraining, yet its effectiveness depends strongly on the calibration data. We propose CoreCalib, a training-free and quantizer-agnostic framework for constructing compact calibration sets that preserve the target medical VQA distribution. CoreCalib stratifies data by clinical question class, identifies representative visual modes using frozen DINOv2 features with UMAP and HDBSCAN, and expands selected images into class-balanced question-answer pairs. On Kvasir-VQA-x1, we evaluate CoreCalib with MASQuant, GPTQ, and QIG using a fixed 128-pair budget. CoreCalib achieves the best METEOR with all three quantizers and the best ROUGE-L with MASQuant and GPTQ. With W4A8 MASQuant, it improves METEOR from 0.5672 with COCO calibration to 0.6234, recovering approximately 41% of the degradation relative to BF16. These results support CoreCalib as a data-centric component for resource-efficient medical VLM deployment. Project page: https://magnusdtd.github.io/CoreCalib/ .

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 CoreCalib，一种无需训练、与量化器无关的校准集构建方法：按临床问题类别分层，用冻结 DINOv2 特征经 UMAP/HDBSCAN 选出代表性视觉模态，再扩展成类别均衡的医学 VQA 问答对，用于低比特 PTQ 压缩。
AI.relevance_reason: 工作重心是量化校准数据选择与部署压缩，未涉及 latent 推理状态、证据获取、停止决策或训练信号分配；其中的聚类选样与 LVR 的表示/证据问题仅有泛泛的「子集选择」相似性，缺乏可核查的具体联系。
